clue.text: Drab regime ultimately established by doctor

definitions.text: Drab regime ultimately established by doctor

indicators.note: by means next to, so the abbreviation for established sits beside the doctor
ultimately points at the final letter of each of the two words Drab and regime

parts.note: EST is the abbreviation for established, as in 'est. 1890' on a shop sign

explanation.surface: A dreary routine a physician has finally laid down for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the dull regime a doctor orders is rest in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed to recover is a tedious treatment that a physician prescribes, which is just what the clue describes.

clue.text: Venetian pro's fit for game

parts.note: a Venetian blind is a window blind of slats
a pro is a hired working man, so pro's gives man's
buff means fit and muscular

explanation.surface: A professional from Venice fit for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Blind man's buff is a children's party game in which a blindfolded player tries to catch the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind man's buff is a traditional children's party pastime involving a blindfolded seeker.

clue.text: Insects paired off across top of trees

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch around the tree letter
off means the letters of paired are out of order
top of in a down clue means the first letter

parts.note: first letter of trees

explanation.surface: Insects pairing up and flying off over the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns paired into DIPERA, which goes across the T from 'top of trees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the order of two-winged insects, including flies, gnats and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Makes containers articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the word for containers is pronounced

parts.note: urns are containers, for tea or ashes

explanation.surface: Manufactures containers with jointed parts, like an articulated lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, as in 'she makes a good salary'.

clue.text: Priests use this relic perhaps in northern land

indicators.note: in means the bone goes inside the name of the land

parts.note: Thule was the ancients' name for the most northerly land
a rib, as a saint's bone, is one example of a holy relic

explanation.surface: Clergy use a sacred relic, maybe in some northern country.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurible is a censer, a metal vessel swung by priests to burn incense during services.

clue.text: Around one, check on really old Muscovite?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the check-with-one part follows the word for really

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: Around means the word for check wraps itself round the numeral

parts.note: to vet is to check over
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone checking on a very old Russian from Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: not every Soviet citizen was a Muscovite, but one from Moscow was a Soviet in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former USSR, whose capital was Moscow, is a Soviet; the USSR no longer exists, hence old.

clue.text: Vessels belonging to chef?

parts.note: Rick Stein is a well-known British TV chef
belonging to gives the possessive 's, as in the chef's own

explanation.surface: Asking whether the pots belong to the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick Stein is a British TV chef; steins are German beer mugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Steins are large earthenware beer mugs, drinking vessels of German origin.

clue.text: Depravity while vicar turned the opposite way

parts.note: vice is depravity or wickedness

indicators.note: turned means the two words are read backwards

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I was leaving'
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: Wickedness while a vicar turned the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses AS + REV to give VERSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is a Latin phrase meaning with the order or relation reversed.

clue.text: Continue feeding a German protein

indicators.note: feeding means the word for continue is put into the German article

parts.note: ein is German for a
to last is to continue or endure

explanation.surface: Carry on giving food to a German to build protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is an elastic fibrous protein found in skin and connective tissue.

clue.text: Bring in from abroad a French badger

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
une is French for a (feminine)

explanation.surface: Importing a French badger from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal, but here it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them with repeated requests, which is what importune means.

clue.text: Opening bridges mechanic has manufactured

indicators.note: bridges means the answer spans the gap between the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of mechanic through has to the start of manufactured

explanation.surface: A repair worker has built something spanning an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridges' looks like what the mechanic built, but it signals letters spanning several words.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep gap or fissure in the ground, an opening in the earth.

clue.text: Inaccurate Armenian chart: it's abysmal

indicators.note: an inaccurate chart is wrongly drawn, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Armenian map is so wrong it's terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abysmal' looks like 'terrible', but here it means of the abyss: the deepest ocean trench.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest part of the world's ocean, an abyss.

clue.text: Imprisonment having stolen university gown

indicators.note: having stolen means the university letter has been taken away from the word

parts.note: duress can mean forcible restraint or imprisonment

explanation.surface: Someone in jail has nicked an academic gown from a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as theft of a university gown; actually the letter for university is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress is a woman's one-piece garment, and a gown is a long formal one.

clue.text: Zero tax on tavern exposed Tory moderniser

indicators.note: on means the zero and tax are placed after the tavern

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
O looks like zero
VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer layer, so Tory loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Tory with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A Conservative reformer proposes no tax on pubs, perhaps then caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovator introduces new methods and ideas, so is someone who modernises.

clue.text: An opportunity to buy cheap barrier for water

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water
a sale is a chance to buy goods at reduced prices

explanation.surface: A cut-price chance to buy a flood barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, 'a dam sale' is a chance to buy a cheap barrier; Adam's ale is an old jokey name for water, the first man having had nothing else to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous idiom for plain drinking water.

clue.text: Wild cats gulping noodle soup, bread and wine

indicators.note: gulping means the rearranged cats swallow the soup
wild means the letters of cats run riot into a new order

parts.note: ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

explanation.surface: Feral cats wolfing noodle soup alongside bread and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns cats into SACT, which takes in RAMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Communion, the Christian rite of consecrated bread and wine, is called the Sacrament.

clue.text: Nutcases operated within intelligence service

indicators.note: within means the word for operated goes inside the agency's letters

parts.note: CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
ran means operated, as of a machine or business

explanation.surface: Lunatics have been running spies inside the CIA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutcases' suggests madmen, but a nut is slang for a head, and the cases of heads are skulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Crania are skulls, the bony cases holding the brain, here called the cases of nuts (heads).

clue.text: Main problem for the Brexiteers

parts.note: main is the sea; the stretch of water between Britain and Ireland caused the post-Brexit border headache

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief', but it is the old word for the sea; the Northern Ireland border question was Brexit's thorniest issue.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea separates Great Britain from the island of Ireland, where the post-Brexit customs border ended up.

clue.text: Wanting Cliff covers to compile

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

indicators.note: covers means just the outside letters of compile are used

parts.note: first and last letters of compile

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard's cover versions being compiled into an album.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, lacking or insufficient, just as wanting means.

clue.text: Strapping below tibia lost finally on the run

indicators.note: below, in a down clue, puts the big word under the final letters
finally points at the last letter of each of tibia and lost

parts.note: strapping means big and burly, so large

explanation.surface: A strapping put on below a broken shin has finally come off.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive at large is free and not yet captured, i.e. escaped.

clue.text: Design area to host mass meal

indicators.note: to host means the joined letters take in the symbol for mass as a guest

parts.note: to create is to design or devise
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Designing a space big enough to hold a large gathering for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon meal of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon repast of scones, cream, jam and a pot of tea.

clue.text: They're regularly on very small stations

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second
regularly means every other letter of They're is taken

parts.note: alternate letters of They're
mini means very small

explanation.surface: They're often on very small railway stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are terminal stations, the end points of railway or bus lines.

clue.text: This group should arguably go on first in 19

definitions.text: This group should arguably go on first in 19

parts.words: This group should arguably go on first in 19
parts.note: a band whose name is the spread that, by the Cornish custom, goes on a scone before the cream

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is CREAM TEA; Devon puts cream first, Cornwall puts the jam first, hence 'arguably'. The band is Paul Weller's 1970s-80s mod trio.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jam were a British punk and mod revival band, and jam is the preserve spread on scones.

clue.text: Releases remains after relative essentially expired

indicators.note: after means the remains come after the relative
the essence or heart of the word has died, so its middle letter goes

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
ashes are the remains after cremation

explanation.surface: Someone frees the ashes of a relative who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially expired' means the middle letter of UNCLE (C) dies away, leaving UNLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to set loose or free, so unleashes and releases are synonyms.

clue.text: Rooks circling are not so commonly seen

indicators.note: circling means the two rook letters go round the word are

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook, so two rooks give two Rs

explanation.surface: Rooks wheeling around are rarely seen birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooks here are chess pieces rather than birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, meaning less frequently found or observed.

clue.text: Egg squashed by short river creature

indicators.note: squashed by, in a down clue, puts the egg under the shortened river
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Rhine is a major European river
O, shaped like an egg

explanation.surface: An egg crushed by a creature beside a short river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino, short for rhinoceros, is a large horned African or Asian animal.

clue.text: Fellow internally reconfigured giant workshop

indicators.note: internally reconfigured means the giant's letters are rearranged inside, its middle pair swapped

parts.note: an ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore

explanation.surface: A fellow inside a huge workshop that has been rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a blacksmith's workshop with a furnace for heating metal.

clue.text: Fair daughter abducted from Asian emperor

parts.note: just means fair

indicators.note: abducted from means the daughter's letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: an Indian is an Asian

explanation.surface: A fair-haired girl has been kidnapped from an Asian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Justinian I was the 6th-century Byzantine emperor famed for his law code.
explanation.definitionFit: Justinian was a ruler of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire.

clue.text: Part of nose mum's unbandaged after a month

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the month

parts.note: Sept is the abbreviation for September

indicators.note: unbandaged means the outer wrapping letters are removed

parts.note: mum's without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Mum's injured nose has had its bandages taken off after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The septum is the partition of cartilage separating the two nostrils.

clue.text: End section of each silo basically rotated

indicators.note: rotated says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a slice cut out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of every grain silo has essentially been turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'section of' unassigned; it signals the letters concealed in the words that follow. 'End' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to put an end to it, formally doing away with it.
